Messages.Author: pallando
Messages.Body:
actually this didn't happen in a v:ekn tournament but in our monthly league.
still i'd like to know how this situation would be handled in a v:ekn
tournament:

4 player table with players A, B, C; and D.

player A threatens player C. he tells him to leave, otherwise he will beat
him.

player C ousts himself, giving player B a victory point and 6 pool, thus
making the situation very bad for player D.

game ends with 1 VP for player D and 3 VP fpr player B.

now the problem:
player C had good chances of ousting D.
player D had good chances of ousting B as well as A if B hadn't gotten his
VP and 6 pool so easily.

how do i solve this problem VPwise?
A didn't get any VP so there is nothing i can take from him.
but C and also B were treated unfairly concerning the VP.

of course some action needs to be taken against A because he threatened
another player. in a tournament he will most probably be sent home. in a
league maybe expelled.

but still the problem with the tournament / league standings remains.

thanks for any help

pallando

If this were to happen in a DCI Magic tournament, the
player would be immediately ejected (I don't know how
that would work in a 4-player game), and the player would
likely be banned from sanctioned events for
at least 3 months, probably much, much longer.

Yes, I know this isn't Magic, but the people over there
have put quite a lot of thought, trial, and error into
how to properly conduct a tournament environment, so
their solutions can be informative, if not instructive.

Did the judge know of the threat during the game,
or only afterward? When you say C self-ousted,
do you mean he got up and left due to the threat?

- Jason Bell

Messages.Author: Wes
Messages.Body:
"pallando" <pall...@gmx.at> wrote

> player A threatens player C. he tells him to leave, otherwise he will beat
> him.

Could you expand on this? Do you mean that one player actually *physically
threatened* another player? There must be more to it than that...

In the case that he did actually physically threaten another player, I'd
probably try to arrange a meeting with all the local players and decide by
consensus whether the threatening player should be invited back...
*irregardless* of tournaments.

If it were a case of the usual Machiavellian threats that pass around a
Jyhad table, no problem... as long as both players recognize that it's
'role-playing' or what-have-you. Personally, any game where I do not feel
comfortable shaking the hands of the players at my table, I would rather
*leave*... and on the odd occasion I have (though not often).

Cheers,
WES

No offense, but in this case... fuck the game. This is *way* beyond bad
sportsmanship.

I'd tell the guy to get lost and if he shows up again, I wouldn't
acknowledge him.

I realize there is rarely a person who can really speak for the rest of the
group, even the so-called 'prince', but the players of your group need to
decide whether they collectively want to condone this behaviour. Presumably,
*you* don't, but considering that two other players apparently had no
problem with it... Frankly, I'm surprised they even finished the game.

Is this guy known for this kind of behaviour? Did he make any attempt to
explain why he did this? Was there any type of settlement after? I'm just
stunned that this kind of shit could even happen. He wouldn't get away with
it here, that's for sure.

Cheers,
WES
